propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui beatum Gabrielem dulcissimae Matris tuae dolores assidue recolere
docuisti, ac per illam sanctitatis et miraculorum gloria sublimasti: da
nobis, ejus intercessione et exemplo; ita Genetricis tuae consociari
fletibus, ut materna ejusdem protectione salvemur: Qui vivis et regnas cum
Deo Patre in unitate.

provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: conclusion length differs: the 1962 prints "Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitate Spiritus Sancti Deus."; the antecedent prints "Qui vi- vis. Communio. Apoc. 3, 20. Ecce sto"; accents, ae/oe ligatures and word division differ throughout; the antecedent reading is an optical text layer and its pointing cannot be trusted at comma level. Corroboration: none reached the 0.55 alignment floor. Recorded limitation: The 1962 reading was settled on the facsimile page image; the antecedent reading is an optical text layer only and its letterforms and pointing were not verified on a page image (the 1862's images are not available to this lane, and the Mame's were not rendered for this entry). What was NOT checked: the Benziger conformed printing was used only as a boundary check on the extraction, never as a reading; no attempt was made to establish which of several possible loci in the antecedent is the 'original' one, since an order is not a contribution. This oration is one the Missal draws from a Common; the antecedent witness may print it at the Common, at another saint's day, or at both. That is a difference of position, not of words.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Salutarem hostiam in memoriam sancti Gabrielis tibi, Domine, offerentes, fac
nos sacrificium mortis tuae rite recolere, ac, meritis perdolentis Virginis,
ejusdem sacrificii fructum copiose percipere: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo
Patre in unitate Spiritus Sancti Deus.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

translations.text: Make us, O Lord, who offer Thee the saving host in memory of St. Gabriel, daily to recall the Sacrifice of Thy death; and by the merits of the sorrowful Virgin abundantly to receive the fruit of the same sacrifice. Who livest.

collatis donis gratias agimus: suscipe propitius per manus gloriosae semper
Virginis Mariae; ex qua carnem illam assumpsisti, cujus in hoc salutari
convivio meruimus gustare dulcedinem: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in
unitate.

translations.text: The thanks which we offer to Thee, O Lord, in the festivity of St. Gabriel, Thy confessor, for the gifts we have received, do Thou graciously receive at the hands of the glorious ever-virgin Mary: of whom Thou didst take that flesh whose sweetness we have deserved to taste in this healthful banquet. Who livest.
